papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of QAOA combining XY-mixers for one-hot constraints with oracle-based indicator-function penalties for inequality constraints, benchmarked against QUBO on Multi-Knapsack and Prosumer problems.

existing.note: The abstract's order-of-magnitude claim is borne out in the body by a measured average speedup of 87 over QUBO only for the instances until Comb3_0; for larger instances the advantage is an extrapolation of a fit, and the authors say the pipeline differences narrowed in TTS compared with the solution-quality results. All results are noiseless simulations.
existing.value: The authors report that the combined architecture gives a better solution quality and probability of sampling the optimal solution than the QUBO formulation, and that the time-to-solution is more than an order of magnitude faster than the baseline methods. In the results they report an average speedup factor of 87 of the QUBO time-to-solution over that of IF+XY across the instances until Comb3_0, and for larger instances the advantage is an extrapolation.

papers.what_it_is: A classical-simulation study of sparse Trotterization, a Trotter-Suzuki variant with coarser time steps across quantum interconnects, on XY and transverse-field Ising spin chains.

existing.note: The result is from noiseless classical simulation of one-dimensional spin chains and is measured against a reference state obtained from uniform Trotterization with a fixed step size, not against the exact solution. The authors say hardware-specific error models are needed to find the optimal tradeoff, and that for the fast Ising quench the fidelity falls rapidly for sparsity of 6 or more.
existing.value: The authors state that, for the models they study, fast local operations on monolithic devices can be leveraged to obtain an overall improved result fidelity even on distributed quantum computers where the use of interconnects is costly. They state that further calculations with hardware specific error models are required to find the optimal tradeoff.
quotes: we show that fast local operations on monolithic devices can be leveraged to obtain an overall improved result fidelity even on distributed quantum computers where the use of interconnects is costly.
Further calculations with hardware specific error models are required to find the optimal tradeoff.

papers.what_it_is: A proposal of the multiple-triangle ansatz (MuTA), a universal quantum neural network native to measurement-based quantum computing, with simulated learning tasks and a photonic hardware-constrained variant.

existing.note: Added detail: homodyne detection gives angles 0 and pi/2, and a T magic state adds pi/4 for universality.

The evidence is numerical simulation on small instances: the gate-learning task uses a two-wire layer, the state classifier uses two-qubit states, and the kernel works on some toy datasets and not on the moons dataset. No hardware run and no comparison with a circuit-model QNN is reported.
existing.value: The authors state that they provided numerical evidence for the practical value of MuTA by learning a universal gate set, a quantum state classifier and a quantum instrument. Their gate-learning demonstration uses MuTA layer (2, 0) learning Haar-random single-qubit gates and the gate IsingXX(π/2), and for classical data they report that their kernel works for circles and blobs but not for moons.
quotes: provided numerical evidence for the practical value of MuTA by learning a universal gate set, a quantum state classifier, and a quantum instrument.
Specifically, we show how MuTA layer (2, 0), see Fig. 1b, learns Haar-random single-qubit gates on the first qubit, as well as the entangling gate IsingXX(π/2).
we find that our kernel can be used for data that does not have a strongly non-linear structure, such as circles and blobs, but not for moons.

assertions.value: The paper states Property 6 (Monotonicity of expressivity): adding layers, adding disconnected wires, or adding admissible triangles together with an extra layer monotonically increases the set of implementable gates. The proof it gives shows weak monotonicity, that the expansions do not reduce the set of implementable gates.

assertions.value: The paper states Property 7 that the graph of any MuTA is 2-colorable, because a graph is 2-colorable if and only if it is bipartite and collecting even columns and odd columns gives a bipartition. papers.title_in_file: Machine-learning based noise characterization and correction on neutral atoms NISQ devices
papers.version_note: arXiv:2306.15628v1, 27 Jun 2023. The text layer holds the paper twice, the second copy used only to check quotes.
papers.what_it_is: A study training ANN and linear-regression models on simulated Pasqal measurements to estimate noise parameters tested on real data, plus a reinforcement-learning pulse correction demonstrated in simulation.

existing.note: The comparison of ANN with linear regression is for one parameter only, the laser intensity fluctuation, on a synthetic validation set; the paper adds that ANNs are more resource intensive. The accuracy gain with atoms and measurements is read from error bars in figures, and no values are given in the text.
existing.value: The authors report that, for predicting the laser intensity fluctuation on the simulated validation set, the errors of the ANN models are always lower than those of linear regression, with the difference more pronounced as the number of atoms and measurements increases, at the cost of more resource-intensive computations, and that the prediction error decreases with the number of atoms in the system.
existing.anchor: Section III-A, p.4-5; Section V, p.7
quotes: In fact, the errors for the ANN models are always lower respect to the errors of linear regression models and the difference is more pronounced increasing the number of atoms and measurements.
ANN are in general more powerful respect to linear regression models (at the cost of more resource-intensive computations).
As expected, the prediction error is decreasing with the number of atoms in the system
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on one noise parameter.

existing.note: The paper hedges it: the basis is one comparison of a 5-atom setting against two concatenated 4-atom settings with the same number of data points, for one parameter on synthetic data, and says 'seems' and 'slightly better'.
existing.value: The authors state that comparing the 5-atom result with the result for two measurements seems to indicate it is more convenient to consider more measurements than to increase the number of atoms, and that it can be slightly better to use multiple measurements of the same setting than measurements of a different setting with the same number of atoms.
quotes: comparing fig. 2(a) with 5 atoms and fig. 2(b) with number of measurements equal to 2, seems to be more convenient to consider more measurements respect to increase the number of atoms of the setting.
can be slightly better to consider multiple measurements of the same setting with the same topology respect to collect measurements of a different setting with the same number of atoms.
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one study; the authors call it an insight.

existing.note: Testing on real data has no ground truth: the predictions are compared with informal a priori values from Pasqal, and the paper says they do not match, with the real data coming from a prototype device. The correction model was trained and tested on a simulation only.
existing.value: The authors state that the characterization models were trained on simulated noisy measurements and tested on real data, that the predicted values on real data do not match those estimated by Pasqal although all 20 models converge to very similar values, and that the noise-correction model was trained on a simulated test setting.
existing.anchor: Section III-B, p.5; Section V, p.7
quotes: We observe that the predicted values do not match those estimated by Pasqal, although all 20 models always converge to very similar values of the predictions.
For the noise correction we trained a RL model to find a correction pulse to counteract the effects of the noise affecting a simulated test setting.
existing.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The paper lists five noise parameters with estimated values it says Pasqal provided informally: laser intensity fluctuation 3%, laser waist 68 micrometres, temperature 30 microkelvin, false positive measurement 3% and false negative measurement 8%.

assertions.value: The authors state that Pasqal has developed a NISQ device called Fresnel based on a neutral atom processor capable of using up to 100 qubits, and that Pasqal registers can hold at most 100 atoms with a minimum distance of 4 micrometres in bidimensional structures within a maximum radius of 50 micrometres.

Future research lines may include the design of QML models for the noise characterization and correction

assertions.value: The authors report that the laser intensity fluctuation predicted from real measurements is close to the estimated 3% for the 2-atom and 5-atom settings, lower for the 3-atom setting, and around 7% for all 4-atom settings and their concatenations, and they say a possible explanation is that the real data were collected while the device was under development.
